title: Cache hierarchy & batch tuning demo - Cartograph Inc.
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Cartograph through Optimize console recommendations for a two-tier cache (session prefix + KV lookahead), batch size tuning, and end-to-end cost simulations. Customer validated current traffic shape (short multi-turn sessions, many small requests) and prioritized predictable latency and encryption-in-transit + at-rest. Action: send sandbox invite, security pack, and run a 48h hit-rate sim with their session distribution.

Priya to run hit-rate simulation with Cartograph session histogram and return simulated cost/latency curves - target 2028-03-13
Alex to share security package (SOC2, data residency, KMS integration notes) and dedicated pricing options - target 2028-03-11
Schedule 30m deep-dive on VPC/on-prem integration if sandbox shows regime requires private deployment - tentative 2028-03-16

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-09
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Daniel Cho (Cartograph Head of ML), Maya Patel (Platform Eng), Liam O'Rourke (CTO)

[00:00] Alex Reed: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick run through the Optimize console, focus on a two-tier cache idea — session prefix plus KV lookahead, and then some batch sizing recs and a cost sim, is that right Daniel?
[00:12] Daniel Cho: yep, that's perfect. quick context — we have a lot of short conversations, ~95% under 6 turns, and many API calls are small, like 20-60 tokens generation. latency matters for us (sub-300ms P95 is ideal), and security is a hard constraint, we need KMS and VPC options.
[00:28] Priya Nair: thanks, that shapes the recommendation — with short sessions you get good prefix cache hit potential but small per-request tokens mean batching becomes tricky, if you batch too aggressively you blow latency. we'll show tradeoffs in the simulator.
[00:42] Maya Patel: one more thing, our current infra is GCP, and we do SAML SSO through Okta; also curious about audit logs and retention for compliance.
[00:50] Alex: absolutely, we'll cover SSO and the audit logs page, and the security pack after. ok let's pull up the console — i'm sharing my screen.

[02:10] Priya: (screen) here is the Optimize workspace, the 'Cache Guidance' panel suggested a two-tier approach: short-lived session prefix caching at the runtime level for immediate reuse of KV tokens, and a KV lookahead layer that prefetches likely continuations for active sessions. recommended TTLs are short for prefix (~30s-2m) and longer for KV depending on session churn.
[02:45] Daniel: real quick, can you quantify "lookahead" — what hit rates do you usually see?
[02:51] Priya: it depends on session homogeneity; for highly templated dialogs we've seen 40-70% KV hit rates in the sim, combined with prefix hits you can push effective token reduction ~30-60% in typical consumer chat apps. but for Cartograph, given your short sessions and many unique contexts, i'd expect midrange, maybe 25-45% overall if we tune TTL and prefetch heuristics.
[03:20] Liam: and how does that interact with batching? we worry that batching will postpone first-byte latency and kill interactivity.
[03:26] Priya: good point — batching reduces per-token cost by amortizing kernel overhead, but increases latency for the first request in a batch. in the console we simulate latency SLOs: with batch size 8 you might see token cost drop 20-30% but P95 latency could jump from 120ms to ~270ms depending on GPU kernel selection and sequence lengths. that's why we recommend adaptive batch windows: small immediate batches for interactive (0-100ms window), and background batching for bulk inference.
[04:05] Daniel: can the runtime route requests differently? like route low-latency customers to dedicated nodes and other traffic to cheaper shared hosted?
[04:12] Alex: yes, smart routing is built-in — you can route by policy. for your case you could pin high-priority endpoints to dedicated pools (predictable latency) and overflow to hosted; Optimize can show cost per 1k tokens for each path.
[04:28] Maya: what's the delta on cost between hosted and dedicated? numbers please.
[04:32] Priya: rough example from the simulator: hosted (on-demand) generation cost baseline X — let's call it $0.18 per 1k tokens for that model profile; dedicated amortized with reserved capacity and better batch utilization could go down to $0.07-$0.10 per 1k depending on utilization. the console runs utilization sensitivity so you can see break-even at ~60-70% GPU utilization.
[04:58] Daniel: okay, that helps. question on encryption — we need customer-managed keys and auditable exports. how does Redwood handle KMS?
[05:04] Alex: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and dedicated customers; we have key-wrap support and can show key rotation logs. audit-log exports are available and you can push to your SIEM. we'll attach the security PDF after the call.
[05:18] Liam: if we go Private (VPC), does the Optimize console still work or is it air-gapped?
[05:23] Priya: for Private we provide a control plane connector; console can be run with a private control plane or via a console agent inside the VPC. there are tradeoffs—some telemetry stays local unless you opt into sending anonymized metrics for cost modeling. we typically recommend a hybrid for initial pilots.

[06:10] Priya: going back to caching mechanics, key detail — the "prefix" cache is basically storing KV cache snippets for repeated opening turns, it reduces recomputation on common prefixes. "KV lookahead" prefetches the next few attention states based on predicted continuations; it's not full stateful sessionization but it gets you a lot of wins for structured dialogs.
[06:45] Daniel: any rough guidance on TTLs? like set prefix TTL to 45s and KV to 10 minutes?
[06:50] Priya: exactly the sort of thing we tune. for your traffic i'd start prefix TTL 30-90s, KV lookahead 5-15m with LRU eviction rules and a small warm pool. the console's heuristic tuner can suggest initial values using your session histogram.
[07:10] Alex: show them the savings sim — Priya do the 3-scenario sim: baseline (no cache, batch=1), moderate cache + batch small, and aggressive prefetch + batch large.
[07:20] Priya: running sim now — input assumptions: avg request tokens 40, avg response 80, 12k requests/day peak 450 qps burst, session length median 3, 95th 8. scenario A baseline cost: $0.18/1k tokens, monthly est $3,900. scenario B (prefix hit 25%, KV 15%, batch size 4 adaptive) cost ~ $2,700 (about 30% savings) but P95 latency ~200ms. scenario C (prefix 40%, KV 35%, batch size 8 heavy for background) cost ~ $1,800 (54% savings) but P95 for interactive-only endpoints goes up — so you'd reserve dedicated pools for those interactive endpoints.
[08:12] Daniel: those are useful. small nit — your transcription says "K V cache" sometimes in docs, do you mean key-value or is that keyed value cache?
[08:18] Priya: sorry for the jargon — we mean key-value state cache, same as KV. some folks say "keev" jokingly.
[08:25] Maya: on implementation, how invasive is the client change? can we instrument with a middleware to record prefixes and suggest TTL?
[08:31] Priya: minimal changes — we provide SDK wrappers that capture prefix tokens and hit metrics. you can also run offline instrumentation: give us your logs and we run an offline analyzer to calculate theoretical cacheable prefix mass and simulate lookahead. that's what we'll do in the sandbox.
[08:50] Liam: if we do lookahead, what's the worst-case extra token cost for mispredictions?
[08:55] Priya: bad prefetches incur extra token cost but they often reduce end-to-end compute because subsequent tokens can reuse the prefetched cache. in extreme misprediction you pay for the extra tokens; the optimizer applies a cost penalty to limit prefetch width. the console sim includes misprediction sensitivity.

[10:05] Alex: switching gears — integration checklist: SSO, KMS, VPC, audit logs, data residency. Daniel, which of those are must-haves for your security review?
[10:14] Daniel: KMS and VPC are musts, SOC2 a must, audit logs preferred. SSO is table stakes. we also need a data residency option for EU customers.
[10:24] Alex: good — we'll include all that in the pack and call out Private deployment options for EU residency.
[10:30] Priya: also note: dedicated zones let you pin models and quantization profiles, it's useful for latency-sensitive workloads — we can pre-warm kernels and maintain warm KV pools to reduce cold-start p95.
[10:45] Maya: do you provide example configs or helm charts for on-prem?
[10:49] Priya: yes, for Private we provide an ops repo with k8s manifests, helm charts and a deployment runbook. we'll include a sanitized example in the sandbox.

[12:10] Daniel: quick commercial question — if we commit to reserved Dedicated for 12 months, what's typical uplift to get down to that $0.07/1k tokens?
[12:18] Alex: it depends on GPU type and commitment; typical 12-month reserved with utilization guarantees and good batching gets you 40-60% off list hosted rates. we'll provide a dedicated pricing sheet tailored to your traffic shape.
[12:30] Liam: and support SLAs? 24/7 for production?
[12:33] Jamal (redwood): our enterprise plan includes 24/7 on-call with pager rotation for severity 1, additional options for runbooks and on-site support are available for Private deployments.

[13:05] Priya: back to tuning — a concrete plan: 1) run offline analyzer to give suggested TTLs and prefetch widths; 2) provision a sandbox with representative load; 3) run 48h sim to observe real hit rates and adjust heuristics; 4) propose Dedicated carve-out for interactive endpoints if latency SLOs require it.
[13:30] Maya: sounds good. how invasive is the SDK change again? our frontend is TypeScript and we prefer minimal client churn.
[13:36] Priya: SDKs are small — a single middleware hook to record prefix keys and flush on session end, and server-side the runtime handles lookup and prefetch. we also provide a proxy option so you can do it with minimal code changes.

[15:00] Daniel: security follow-up: can we KMS wrap per-customer keys in the Private model? we need per-tenant key separation for compliance.
[15:06] Alex: yes — per-customer keying is supported in Private and Dedicated for enterprise, we can show the KMS integration guide in the pack.
[15:12] Liam: any red flags we should watch for in the sim? like when caches add more variability?
[15:17] Priya: watch for cache cold-starts during burst traffic and eviction churn with very long tail unique sessions. that's where hybrid sessionization (short prefix TTLs + smaller KV warm pool) helps. also watch for tokenization mismatch between your clients and the runtime which can reduce hit-rate — we can detect that in the analyzer.

[17:05] Alex: ok recap and next steps — we provision the sandbox, Priya runs the sim with your histogram, Alex will send security + pricing. any final Qs?
[17:18] Daniel: quick one — do you have references or a similar customer example we can talk to?
[17:22] Alex: we have a customer in digital commerce that used the same two-tier and saw 48% cost reduction; we'll anonymize the case study and include a short write up.
[17:30] Maya: perfect. thanks.

[18:00] (informal banter and small talk)
[20:00] End of transcript notes: occasional transcription glitches: "K V" sometimes written as separate letters, some proper nouns miscaptured (e.g., customer internal service names). The transcript was reviewed by Redwood AE for accuracy.
